syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

chapters.title: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence

topics.title: Colonial rule and the low level of economic development

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how colonial economic policy turned India into a supplier of raw materials and a consumer of British finished goods.
Identify the estimators of national and per capita income in the colonial period and the growth rates they found.
Explain the causes of agricultural stagnation and low productivity under British rule.
Analyse how the zamindari system and its revenue terms harmed cultivators.
Evaluate why commercialisation of agriculture did little to improve farmers' condition.
State the two-fold motive behind the systematic de-industrialisation of India.
Describe the slow growth of modern industry and the absence of a capital goods industry before independence.

topics.title: Foreign trade and the drain of wealth

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the composition and direction of India's foreign trade under colonial rule.
Explain why India's export surplus led to the drain of Indian wealth.
Recall the first census and the stages of demographic transition in British India.
Interpret the literacy, mortality and life-expectancy figures of the colonial period.
State the shares of the workforce in agriculture, manufacturing and services before independence.
Analyse the regional variation in occupational structure across presidencies and states.

topics.title: Infrastructure and the state of the economy at independence

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the real motives behind colonial development of roads, railways, waterways and communications.
Summarise the economic challenges facing India at independence.

topics.title: Economic Systems and the Beginning of Planning

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish how capitalist, socialist and mixed economies answer what, how and for whom to produce.
Describe India's choice of a mixed economy, the Planning Commission and Mahalanobis's role in planning.

topics.title: The Goals of Five Year Plans

concepts.learning_objective: Explain growth and modernisation as goals of planning.
Explain self-reliance and equity as goals of planning and possible conflicts among goals.
Interpret India's peculiar structural change with a large service sector by 1990.
Explain the abolition of intermediaries and the incentive effect of land to the tiller.
Explain land ceiling legislation and why land reforms had limited success.
Describe the green revolution, its phases, requirements and risks.
Explain marketed surplus and its effect on food prices and procurement.
Evaluate the arguments for and against agricultural subsidies.

topics.title: Industrial Development: Public Sector, IPR 1956 and Small-Scale Industry

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the state took a leading role in industrial development.
Describe the three categories of IPR 1956 and the industrial licensing system.
Explain the definition and protection of small-scale industries.

topics.title: Trade Policy and the Effects of Policies (1950-1990)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain import substitution and protection through tariffs and quotas.
Evaluate the achievements and shortcomings of industrial and trade policies during 1950-1990.

chapters.title: LIBERALISATION, PRIVATISATION AND GLOBALISATION: AN APPRAISAL

topics.title: Background of the 1991 Crisis and the New Economic Policy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the fiscal and external causes of India's 1991 economic crisis.
Distinguish between short-term stabilisation measures and long-term structural reform measures of the NEP.
Describe how industrial licensing, reservation and price controls were relaxed after 1991.
Explain the changes in the role of the RBI and in direct and indirect taxes under the reforms.
Explain rupee devaluation and the removal of quantitative restrictions and tariffs in trade policy.
Define privatisation and disinvestment and state the government's reasons for them.
Explain why selected PSEs were given maharatna, navratna and miniratna status.
Explain outsourcing as an outcome of globalisation and why India became an outsourcing destination.
Describe the origin, aims and India's role in the World Trade Organisation.

topics.title: Indian Economy during Reforms: An Assessment

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret post-reform trends in GDP growth, foreign investment and foreign exchange reserves.
Evaluate the criticisms of reforms relating to agriculture, industry, disinvestment and fiscal policy.
Explain how human resources are turned into human capital through investment.
Identify the economic and non-economic benefits that make people seek education.
Explain why spending on education and health is a source of human capital formation.
Explain why firms invest in on-the-job training and expect workers to stay afterwards.
Explain how expenditure on migration and on market information forms human capital.
Distinguish physical and human capital in terms of tangibility, separability and mobility.
Compare the depreciation and the private and social benefits of the two forms of capital.
Explain how human capital raises labour productivity and the ability to absorb new technology.
Evaluate the evidence on the link between human capital and economic growth, including two-way causality.
Interpret the indicators of education, health and income in Table 4.1.
Distinguish human capital (people as a means) from human development (people as ends in themselves).
Discuss whether IT-based services can make India a knowledge economy and lead to human development.
Explain why government must intervene in the education and health service markets.
Identify the organisations that facilitate institutions in the education and health sectors.
Interpret education expenditure as a share of total government expenditure and of GDP.
Recall the recommendations, acts and cess aimed at expanding education in India.
Assess why education for all remains a distant goal in India.
Explain the need to promote women's education in India using literacy data.
Analyse the steep education pyramid and unemployment among educated youth.

topics.title: Meaning and need of rural development

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what rural development covers and the key areas needing fresh initiatives.
Explain why agricultural growth slowed after 1991 and how it affects rural development.

topics.title: Rural credit and the banking system

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the multi-agency institutions of rural credit and the role of NABARD.
Explain how SHGs and micro-credit fill gaps in formal rural credit.
Evaluate the achievements and weaknesses of rural banking, including Jan-Dhan Yojana.
Describe the four government measures to improve agricultural marketing.
Identify emerging alternate marketing channels and assess contract farming.
Explain the two aspects of diversification and why it is needed.
Distinguish dynamic non-farm sub-sectors from those lacking infrastructure.
Describe the role of livestock and Operation Flood in rural livelihoods.

topics.title: Fisheries, horticulture and IT as livelihood options

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the structure and problems of the Indian fisheries sector.
Explain the contribution of horticulture to output, employment and livelihoods.
Assess the role of information technology in rural development and food security.
Explain the meaning and benefits of organic farming for sustainable development.
Evaluate the challenges in popularising organic farming in India.

chapters.title: Employment: Growth, Informalisation and Other Issues

concepts.learning_objective: Explain economic activities as those activities that contribute to the gross national product.
Identify who counts as a worker, including the self-employed, helpers and those temporarily absent from work.
Evaluate why unpaid household and farm work of women leads to under-estimation of women workers.
Define and calculate the worker-population ratio.
Interpret differences in worker-population ratio between rural and urban areas and between men and women.
Distinguish self-employed workers, casual wage labourers and regular salaried employees.
Interpret the distribution of workers by status across gender and region.

topics.title: Employment in Firms, Factories and Offices

concepts.learning_objective: Classify the eight industrial divisions into the primary, secondary and service sectors.
Interpret the distribution of the workforce across sectors by region and sex.

topics.title: Growth and Changing Structure of Employment

concepts.learning_objective: Explain jobless growth as a widening gap between GDP growth and employment growth.
Analyse the shift of the workforce from farm to non-farm work over five decades.
Explain casualisation of the workforce and why it makes workers vulnerable.
Classify establishments and workers into the formal and informal sectors.
Describe the conditions of informal sector workers and the effects of informalisation.
Distinguish open, disguised and seasonal unemployment.
Identify how unemployment is defined and the sources of unemployment data in India.
Distinguish direct and indirect employment generation by the government, including MGNREGA.
Define environment and distinguish its biotic and abiotic elements.
Identify the four functions of the environment and the types of resources it supplies.
Explain why environmental problems have become critical through the reversal of the supply-demand relationship.
Describe the causes and effects of global warming and ozone depletion and the related international agreements.

topics.title: State of India's environment: resources and land degradation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify India's major natural resource endowments and its priority environmental issues.
Explain the causes and extent of land degradation in India.

topics.title: Pollution in India and pollution control

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the sources of air pollution in India, especially vehicular emissions.
Describe the role of the pollution control boards and people's movements such as Appiko.
State the UNCED/Brundtland definition of sustainable development and its key phrases.
Apply Herman Daly's conditions for achieving sustainable development.
Explain the environmental advantages of wind, solar and mini-hydel power over thermal and hydro power.
Explain how LPG, gobar gas and CNG reduce pollution in rural and urban areas.

topics.title: Strategies: traditional knowledge, biocomposting and biopest control

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the value of traditional knowledge and practices such as indigenous healthcare for sustainability.
Explain how biocomposting and biopest control reduce the harm caused by agro-chemicals.

chapters.title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why nations form regional and global economic groupings.
Explain why developing countries study the development strategies of their neighbours.
Contrast the political set-ups of India, Pakistan and China.
Recall when India, Pakistan and China began planned development.
Describe China's Great Leap Forward, communes and the 1978 reforms.
Trace the sequence of Pakistan's economic policies.
Compare population size and density of the three countries.
Explain the one-child norm and its implications for China.
Interpret sex ratio, fertility and urbanisation data for the three countries.
Compare GDP size and growth rates of India, China and Pakistan.
Interpret the sectoral shares of GVA and workforce in the three countries.
Distinguish China's classical pattern of structural change from that of India and Pakistan.
Compare India, China and Pakistan on selected human development indicators.
Explain the meaning and importance of liberty indicators.

topics.title: Development strategies: an appraisal and conclusion

concepts.learning_objective: Recall when and why reforms were introduced in the three countries.
Evaluate the factors behind China's rapid growth and human development.
Analyse the reasons for Pakistan's slowdown and re-emergence of poverty.
